chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Salt, from Abdullah ibn al-Salt, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),
regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «and mention Allah in limited number of days». He said: The known and the limited are one, and they are the days of al-Tashriq.
ai.seo_question: What are the 'limited number of days' mentioned in the Quran identified as in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the exegetical nuance between the 'known days' and 'limited days' mentioned in the Quran, identifying them specifically as the Days of Tashriq. This interpretation underscores the ritual significance of the 11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah as a distinct period for remembrance and sacrifice, linking linguistic precision with liturgical practice in Shia jurisprudence.
